concerns.text: The 7‑dimensional static feature set (node count, edge count, mean degree, max degree, avg shortest‑path, recursion depth, external‑call count) may not fully capture the semantic properties that determine pass/fail outcomes. Without justification that these graph‑level metrics are sufficient proxies for program correctness, the construct validity of the predictor is questionable.

The plan cites a total of ~3.7 k patches but provides no analysis of class balance (pass vs. fail) or of the distribution across the two source datasets. An imbalanced label distribution could severely reduce statistical power and inflate variance of the AUC estimate.

Language (Python vs. C++) and dataset origin (SWE‑Gym vs. Multi‑SWE‑RL) are not modelled as covariates or stratified during splitting. These factors could act as confounds, attributing predictive performance to static features when differences are actually driven by language‑specific or dataset‑specific characteristics.

Unparsable patches are logged and skipped, but the impact of this exclusion on the representativeness of the sample is not discussed. Systematically dropping syntactically problematic patches may bias the analysis toward easier code, inflating the apparent predictive power of static features.
